title: M39, NGC 7092
caption: The open star cluster M39 (NGC 7092), imaged by the WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This picture shows M39, a loose and widely spaced open cluster of stars in the constellation Cygnus. By astronomical standards it is quite close to Earth.

An open cluster is a group of stars born together from the same cloud of gas, still traveling loosely as a family. M39 has around 30 members and is thought to be two to three hundred million years old.

Open clusters do not last forever. Over time, gravitational nudges from passing stars and clouds tend to pull their members apart, so the stars gradually drift away and join the general population of the galaxy. Studying clusters of known age like M39 helps astronomers compare how stars of different masses change as they grow older, because all the members started out at roughly the same time.
scale: M39 lies about 800 light-years away, according to NOIRLab.

understand.summary: The WIYN 0.9-meter Telescope's Mosaic camera took visible-light frames through B, V and R filters. The source does not say which color each filter was assigned.

explore: The image combines 33 frames in B, V and R colors taken with the Mosaic camera on Kitt Peak's WIYN 0.9-meter telescope, outside Tucson, Arizona, during the night of September 15th, 2003. The camera uses eight separate CCD chips, so small shifts between exposures, called dithers, fill in the gaps between them.
